S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, explosion, or injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary account of known facts. Other confirmed overheating events must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers—within 24 hours for fires, thermal runaway, or injury, and within 5 business days for other confirmed overheating events—and provide any immediate safety steps.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and an adequately sized representative sample before sale, at least every two years thereafter, and after a material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Exceeding the limit requires corrective action and regulator review, but does not automatically require withdrawal of units already in service, suspend new sales, or impose a permanent market ban.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must support a secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear instructions for customers and emergency responders. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must offer an upgrade or other technically feasible means of remote shut-off within 6 years.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New battery systems must include built-in fire suppression. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall of any model whose thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 per 100,000 installed units in a year, notify the relevant regulator and affected customers, and provide safe-use or shutdown instructions while the recall is implemented. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, and corrective actions, using the timelines in S1.

document.section_notes: S1 is strong on deadlines (24 h serious, 5 business days other, 24 h/5 business day customer notice) but scope is limited to confirmed overheating events for the non-serious tier, which is merely acceptable. S2 keeps the 55 °C test and 5% limit and gives numeric failure rates to purchasers (satisfying HC-1) without public publication (satisfying NW-1), but exceeding the limit triggers only corrective action and regulator review—sales never have to stop—so S2 falls to weakened and clearly favours Northwind. S3 sets a 6-year retrofit deadline (within NW-2, acceptable), S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months (within HC-2, acceptable), and S5 imposes an immediate mandatory recall at 8/100k with no phase-in, which hits Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9/100k) directly.
